mishnayos.summary: The Torah was handed down from Moshe at Har Sinai, from one generation to the next. The Men of the Great Assembly taught three things: judge carefully, teach many students, and make a fence around the Torah.

chunks.en: Moshe received the Torah from Sinai,

words.note: The mountain where Hashem gave the Torah.

chunks.en: and he passed it on to Yehoshua,
and Yehoshua passed it to the Elders,

words.note: The leaders who lived after Yehoshua.

chunks.en: and the Elders to the Prophets,
and the Prophets passed it on to the Men of the Great Assembly.

words.note: A group of 120 great Sages at the start of the second Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: They said three things:
Be patient when you judge,
chunks.explain: Take your time before deciding a case.

chunks.en: and set up many students,
and make a fence for the Torah.
chunks.explain: Extra rules that keep us far from doing an aveirah.

mishnayos.summary: Shimon HaTzaddik teaches that the world stands on three things: learning Torah, serving Hashem, and doing kindness.

chunks.he: שִׁמְעוֹן הַצַּדִּיק הָיָה מִשְּׁיָרֵי כְנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה.
chunks.en: Shimon HaTzaddik was one of the last of the Men of the Great Assembly.
He used to say:
The world stands on three things:
on the Torah, and on avodah,
chunks.explain: Avodah is serving Hashem with korbanos in the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: and on doing kindness.

mishnayos.summary: Antignos teaches that we should serve Hashem because we love Him, not to get a reward, and that we should always have fear of Heaven.

chunks.he: אַנְטִיגְנוֹס אִישׁ סוֹכוֹ קִבֵּל מִשִּׁמְעוֹן הַצַּדִּיק.
chunks.en: Antignos of Socho received the Torah from Shimon HaTzaddik.
He used to say:

chunks.he: אַל תִּהְיוּ כַעֲבָדִים הַמְשַׁמְּשִׁין אֶת הָרַב
chunks.en: Do not be like servants who serve their master
in order to get a reward.

chunks.he: אֶלָּא הֱווּ כַעֲבָדִים הַמְשַׁמְּשִׁין אֶת הָרַב
chunks.en: Instead, be like servants who serve their master
not in order to get a reward.
And let the fear of Heaven be upon you.

mishnayos.summary: Yosi ben Yoezer teaches: let your house be a meeting place for Torah scholars, sit at their feet, and drink in their words like a thirsty person.

chunks.he: יוֹסֵי בֶן יוֹעֶזֶר אִישׁ צְרֵדָה וְיוֹסֵי בֶן
chunks.en: Yosi ben Yoezer of Tzereidah and Yosi ben Yochanan of Yerushalayim
received the Torah from them.

chunks.he: יוֹסֵי בֶן יוֹעֶזֶר אִישׁ צְרֵדָה אוֹמֵר,
chunks.en: Yosi ben Yoezer of Tzereidah says:
Let your house be a meeting place for the Sages,
and sit in the dust of their feet,
chunks.explain: Sit close to them, even on the floor, to learn.

chunks.en: and drink their words with thirst.

mishnayos.summary: Yosi ben Yochanan teaches to keep your house open wide for guests and to treat the poor like family. He also warns not to spend too much time in idle chatter, because it pulls a person away from Torah.

chunks.he: יוֹסֵי בֶן יוֹחָנָן אִישׁ יְרוּשָׁלַיִם אוֹמֵר,
chunks.en: Yosi ben Yochanan of Yerushalayim says:
Let your house be open wide,
and let poor people be like members of your house,
and do not talk too much with a woman.
chunks.explain: Do not waste time in idle chatter.

chunks.en: They said this even about his own wife,
so all the more so about his friend's wife.
From here the Sages said:
any time a person talks too much
idle talk with a woman,
he brings trouble on himself,
and he stops learning Torah,
and in the end he will get Gehinnom.

words.note: The place where wicked people are punished after they die.

mishnayos.summary: Yehoshua ben Perachyah teaches: get yourself a teacher, get yourself a friend, and judge every person in a good way.

chunks.en: Yehoshua ben Perachyah and Nittai of Arbel
received the Torah from them.
Yehoshua ben Perachyah says:
Make for yourself a teacher,
and get yourself a friend,
and judge every person
in a good way.
chunks.explain: When you are not sure, think the best about what he did.

mishnayos.summary: Nittai of Arbel teaches: stay away from a bad neighbor, don't make friends with a wicked person, and don't think that bad people won't be punished.

chunks.en: Nittai of Arbel says:
Keep far from a bad neighbor,
and do not join together with a wicked person,
and do not give up on punishment.
chunks.explain: Don't think the wicked will never be punished.

mishnayos.summary: Yehudah ben Tabbai teaches judges to be fair: don't help one side argue, be careful of both sides during the case, and once they accept the judgment, see them both as good people.

chunks.en: Yehudah ben Tabbai and Shimon ben Shetach
received the Torah from them.
Yehudah ben Tabbai says:
Do not make yourself like the lawyers who coach people.
chunks.explain: A judge must not teach one side what to say.

chunks.en: And when the two sides of a case stand before you,
let them be in your eyes like wicked people.
chunks.explain: Watch both sides carefully.

chunks.en: And when they leave you,
let them be in your eyes like innocent people,
once they have accepted the judgment.

mishnayos.summary: Shimon ben Shetach teaches judges to question witnesses carefully, but to be careful with their words so the witnesses don't learn from them how to lie.

chunks.en: Shimon ben Shetach says:
Ask the witnesses many questions,
and be careful with your words,
or else they may learn from them how to lie.

mishnayos.summary: Shemayah teaches: love work, dislike being in charge of others, and don't try to get close to the rulers.

chunks.en: Shemayah and Avtalyon received the Torah from them.
Shemayah says:
Love work,
and hate being a ruler over others,
and do not make yourself known to the government.

mishnayos.summary: Avtalyon warns teachers to be very careful with their words, so students don't learn something wrong and Hashem's Name gets disgraced.

chunks.en: Avtalyon says:
Sages, be careful with your words,
or else you may deserve to be sent into exile
and be exiled to a place of bad water,
chunks.explain: Bad water means wrong teachings.

chunks.en: and the students who come after you will drink and die,
and Hashem's Name will be disgraced.

mishnayos.summary: Hillel teaches us to be like the students of Aharon: love peace and run after peace, love people and bring them close to the Torah.

chunks.en: Hillel and Shammai received the Torah from them.
Hillel says:
Be one of the students of Aharon,

words.note: Moshe's brother, the first Kohen Gadol.

chunks.en: loving peace and chasing after peace,
loving people and bringing them close to the Torah.

mishnayos.summary: Hillel teaches in Aramaic: someone who chases after a big name loses it, someone who doesn't grow in learning shrinks, and someone who uses the crown of Torah for himself will be lost.

chunks.en: He used to say:
One who makes his name big,
loses his name.
And one who does not add to his learning,
will come to an end. And one who does not learn,
deserves death.
And one who uses the crown of Torah for himself will pass away.

mishnayos.summary: Hillel teaches: if I don't take care of myself, who will? If I only care about myself, what am I? And if not now, when?

chunks.en: He used to say:
If I am not for myself,
who will be for me?
And when I am only for myself,
what am I?
And if not now, when?

mishnayos.summary: Shammai teaches: set a fixed time for Torah, say little and do a lot, and greet every person with a cheerful face.

chunks.en: Shammai says:
Make your Torah learning fixed.
Say a little and do a lot,
and greet every person
with a cheerful face.

mishnayos.summary: Rabban Gamliel teaches: get yourself a teacher, keep away from doubt, and don't give maaser by guessing.

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel used to say:
Make for yourself a teacher,
and get away from doubt,
chunks.explain: Ask a teacher instead of guessing.

chunks.en: and do not often give maaser by guessing.
chunks.explain: Measure exactly how much to give.

words.note: A tenth of the crops, given as a gift.

mishnayos.summary: Shimon, the son of Rabban Gamliel, teaches that being quiet is best, that doing is more important than learning about it, and that talking too much brings sin.

chunks.en: Shimon his son says:
All my days I grew up among the Sages,

chunks.he: וְלֹא מָצָאתִי לַגּוּף טוֹב אֶלָּא שְׁתִיקָה.
chunks.en: and I found nothing better for a person than silence.
And learning is not the main thing,
but doing.
And whoever talks too much
brings sin.

mishnayos.summary: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel teaches that the world stays standing on three things: justice, truth and peace.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
The world stays standing on three things:

chunks.he: עַל הַדִּין וְעַל הָאֱמֶת וְעַל הַשָּׁלוֹם,
chunks.en: on justice, and on truth, and on peace,
as it says (Zechariah 8): Truth
and judgment of peace, judge in your gates.

mishnayos.summary: Rebbi teaches us to choose a good path, to be careful with every mitzvah, small or big, and to remember that Hashem sees and hears everything we do.

chunks.en: Rebbi says:

words.note: Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi, who put together the Mishnah.

chunks.he: אֵיזוֹהִי דֶרֶךְ יְשָׁרָה שֶׁיָּבֹר לוֹ הָאָדָם,
chunks.en: Which is the right path that a person should choose for himself?
Whatever brings honor to the one who does it

words.en: to the one who does it

chunks.en: and brings him honor from other people.
And be as careful with a light mitzvah as with a heavy one,
because you do not know the reward
for each of the mitzvos.

chunks.he: וֶהֱוֵי מְחַשֵּׁב הֶפְסֵד מִצְוָה כְּנֶגֶד שְׂכָרָהּ,
chunks.en: And weigh the loss of a mitzvah against its reward,
chunks.explain: What you give up for a mitzvah is small next to its reward.

chunks.en: and the gain of an aveirah against its loss.
Look at three things
and you will not come to sin:
Know what is above you:
an eye that sees and an ear that hears,
and all your deeds are written in a book.

mishnayos.summary: Rabban Gamliel teaches that Torah learning goes well together with working for a living, and that people who work for the community should do it for the sake of Heaven.

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel, the son of
Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi, says:

words.note: The leader of the Jewish people.

chunks.he: יָפֶה תַלְמוּד תּוֹרָה עִם דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ,
chunks.en: Torah learning is beautiful together with a way of earning a living,
because working hard at both makes a person forget sin.
And any Torah that has no work with it
will in the end stop, and it pulls along sin.
And all who work for the community
should work with them for the sake of Heaven,

chunks.he: שֶׁזְּכוּת אֲבוֹתָם מְסַיַּעְתָּן וְצִדְקָתָם עוֹמֶדֶת לָעַד.
chunks.en: because the merit of their fathers helps them, and their goodness lasts forever.
And you, I will give you a lot of reward,
as if you had done it all yourselves.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah warns us to be careful with rulers, because they are only friendly when it helps them, and they don't stand by a person when he is in trouble.

chunks.en: Be careful with the rulers,
because they only bring a person close
for their own needs.
They look like friends when it is good for them,

chunks.he: וְאֵין עוֹמְדִין לוֹ לָאָדָם בִּשְׁעַת דָּחְקוֹ:
chunks.en: but they do not stand by a person when he is in trouble.

mishnayos.summary: Rabban Gamliel teaches to do what Hashem wants as if it were what you want. Hillel teaches not to separate from the community, not to be too sure of yourself, not to judge others too fast, and not to push off learning until later.

chunks.en: He used to say:
Do His will as if it were your will,
so that He will do your will as if it were His will.
Put aside your will because of His will,

chunks.he: כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּבַטֵּל רְצוֹן אֲחֵרִים מִפְּנֵי רְצוֹנֶךָ.
chunks.en: so that He will put aside what others want because of what you want.
Hillel says:
Do not separate yourself from the community,

chunks.he: וְאַל תַּאֲמִין בְּעַצְמְךָ עַד יוֹם מוֹתְךָ,
chunks.en: and do not trust yourself until the day you die,
chunks.explain: Even a good person can still go wrong.

chunks.en: and do not judge your friend
until you are in his place.

chunks.he: וְאַל תֹּאמַר דָּבָר שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִשְׁמֹעַ,
chunks.en: And do not say something that cannot be understood,
saying it will be understood in the end.
And do not say: When I have free time I will learn,
because maybe you will not have free time.

mishnayos.summary: Hillel teaches what different kinds of people cannot do: someone with no learning can't fear sin properly, a shy person can't learn, and an impatient person can't teach. Where there is no one to lead, try to be the leader.

chunks.en: He used to say:
An empty person cannot fear sin,

words.note: Someone with no learning and no good ways.

chunks.en: and an unlearned person cannot be truly pious,

words.note: Am ha'aretz: someone who did not learn.

chunks.en: and a shy person cannot learn,
and an impatient person cannot teach,
and not everyone who does a lot of business becomes wise.
And in a place where there are no men,
try to be a man.
chunks.explain: Where no one is acting right, you be the one to act right.

mishnayos.summary: Hillel saw a skull floating on the water and taught that Hashem pays people back measure for measure.

chunks.en: He also saw one skull
that was floating on top of the water.
He said to it:
Because you drowned others,
they drowned you. And in the end, those who drowned you will be drowned.

mishnayos.summary: Hillel teaches that having more things can bring more trouble, but more Torah, learning, advice and tzedakah bring more good. A good name and Torah are things a person truly gets for himself.

chunks.en: He used to say:
One who adds flesh
adds worms.
chunks.explain: Eating too much just makes more for the worms in the grave.

chunks.en: One who adds possessions
adds worry.
One who adds wives
adds witchcraft.
One who adds maidservants
adds bad behavior.
One who adds servants
adds stealing.
One who adds Torah
adds life.
One who adds sitting and learning

words.note: Sitting and learning in the yeshivah.

chunks.en: adds wisdom.
One who adds advice
adds understanding.
One who adds tzedakah
adds peace.
One who gets a good name
gets it for himself.
One who gets words of Torah for himself
gets for himself life in the World to Come.

mishnayos.summary: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai teaches not to take credit for learning a lot of Torah, because that is what we were made for. He praises each of his five great students.

chunks.en: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai
received the Torah from Hillel and from Shammai.
He used to say:
If you learned a lot of Torah,
do not take the credit for yourself,
because that is what you were created for.
He had five students,
Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai,
and these are they:
Rabbi Eliezer ben Hurkenos,
and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananyah,
and Rabbi Yosi the Kohen,
and Rabbi Shimon ben Nesanel,
and Rabbi Elazar ben Arach.
He used to list their praises:
Rabbi Eliezer ben Hurkenos
is a sealed pit that does not lose a drop.
chunks.explain: He remembers everything he learns.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananyah:
how fortunate is the mother who gave birth to him.

words.en: the one who gave birth to him

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosi the Kohen
is pious. Rabbi Shimon ben Nesanel

words.note: A chasid: someone who does even more than he must.

chunks.en: fears sin.
And Rabbi Elazar ben Arach
is a spring that keeps getting stronger.
chunks.explain: He keeps coming up with new ideas.

chunks.en: He used to say:
If all the Sages
of Israel were on one side of a scale,
and Eliezer ben Hurkenos on the other side,
he would outweigh them all.
Abba Shaul says in his name:
If all the Sages of Israel were

chunks.he: בְּכַף מֹאזְנַיִם וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן הוֹרְקְנוֹס
chunks.en: on one side of a scale, and Rabbi Eliezer ben Hurkenos
was with them too,

chunks.he: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲרָךְ בְּכַף שְׁנִיָּה,
chunks.en: and Rabbi Elazar ben Arach on the other side,
he would outweigh them all.

mishnayos.summary: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai asked his students what is the best path for a person and what is the worst. He agreed most with Rabbi Elazar: a good heart, and the opposite, a bad heart.

chunks.en: He said to them:
Go out and see which is the good path
that a person should stick to.
Rabbi Eliezer says:
A good eye.
chunks.explain: Being happy for others and wishing them well.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
A good friend.
Rabbi Yosi says:
A good neighbor.
Rabbi Shimon says:
One who sees what will come.
chunks.explain: He thinks ahead about what will happen.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar says:
A good heart.
He said to them:
I like the words
of Elazar ben Arach more than your words,
because your words are included in his words.

chunks.he: אָמַר לָהֶם צְאוּ וּרְאוּ אֵיזוֹהִי דֶרֶךְ רָעָה
chunks.en: He said to them: Go out and see which is the bad path
that a person should keep away from.
Rabbi Eliezer says:
A bad eye.
Rabbi Yehoshua says:
A bad friend.
Rabbi Yosi says:
A bad neighbor.
Rabbi Shimon says:
One who borrows and does not pay back.
Borrowing from a person
is like borrowing from Hashem, blessed is He,
as it says (Tehillim 37): One who borrows,
a wicked one, does not pay back,
but a tzaddik is kind and gives.
chunks.explain: Hashem, the Tzaddik, pays back for him.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar says:
A bad heart.
He said to them:
I like the words
of Elazar ben Arach more than your words,
because your words are included in his words.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Eliezer teaches: care about your friend's honor like your own, don't get angry easily, do teshuvah every day, and stay close to the Sages but treat them with great respect.

chunks.en: They each said three things.
Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.he: יְהִי כְבוֹד חֲבֵרְךָ חָבִיב עָלֶיךָ כְּשֶׁלָּךְ,
chunks.en: Let your friend's honor be as dear to you as your own,
and do not get angry easily.
And do teshuvah one day before you die.
chunks.explain: Nobody knows when he will die, so do teshuvah every day.

chunks.he: וֶהֱוֵי מִתְחַמֵּם כְּנֶגֶד אוּרָן שֶׁל חֲכָמִים,
chunks.en: And warm yourself by the fire of the Sages,
but be careful with their coals so you don't get burned,
chunks.explain: Treat them with great respect.

chunks.en: because their bite is the bite of a fox,
and their sting is the sting of a scorpion,
and their hiss is the hiss of a snake,
and all their words are like burning coals.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Yehoshua teaches that a bad eye, the yetzer hara, and hating people take a person out of the world.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
A bad eye,
chunks.explain: Jealousy, wanting what others have.

chunks.en: and the yetzer hara,
and hating people,
take a person out of the world.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Yosi teaches: care about your friend's money like your own, work hard to learn Torah because you don't get it automatically, and do everything for the sake of Heaven.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosi says:

chunks.he: יְהִי מָמוֹן חֲבֵרְךָ חָבִיב עָלֶיךָ כְּשֶׁלָּךְ,
chunks.en: Let your friend's money be as dear to you as your own,
and get yourself ready to learn Torah,
because it is not an inheritance for you.
chunks.explain: You don't get it from your father; you must work for it.

chunks.en: And let all your deeds be for the sake of Heaven.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Shimon teaches to be careful with saying Shema and davening, to daven from the heart and ask Hashem for mercy, and not to think of yourself as wicked.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says:
Be careful with saying Shema and with davening.
And when you daven,
do not make your tefillah a fixed habit,
chunks.explain: Don't just say the words like a chore.

chunks.en: but ask for mercy and beg before
Hashem, blessed is He,
as it says (Yoel 2): For He is kind
and merciful, slow to anger, and full of
kindness, and He changes His mind about bad things.
And do not be wicked in your own eyes.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Elazar teaches: learn Torah with energy, know how to answer someone who mocks the Torah, and remember that you work for Hashem, who will surely pay you.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar says:
Be busy and eager to learn Torah,
and know what to answer an apikores.

words.note: Someone who makes fun of the Torah.

chunks.en: And know before Whom you work.
And your Employer can be trusted
to pay you the reward for your work.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Tarfon compares life to a work day: the time is short, there is a lot to do, the reward is great, and the Master is pushing.

chunks.en: Rabbi Tarfon says:
The day is short and there is a lot of work,
and the workers are lazy,
and the pay is great,
and the Master of the house is pushing.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Tarfon teaches that you don't have to finish all the work, but you may not stop trying. Hashem will surely pay a great reward to those who learn, in the World to Come.

chunks.en: He used to say:
It is not your job to finish the work,

chunks.he: וְלֹא אַתָּה בֶן חוֹרִין לִבָּטֵל מִמֶּנָּה.
chunks.en: but you are not free to stop doing it.
If you learned a lot of Torah,
they give you a lot of reward.
And your Employer can be trusted
to pay you the reward for your work.
And know that the reward
of tzaddikim is in the time to come.

mishnayos.summary: Akavya ben Mahalalel teaches that thinking about three things keeps us from sin: where we come from, where we are going, and that one day we will have to stand before Hashem, the King of kings.

chunks.en: Akavya ben Mahalalel says:
Look at three things
and you will not come to sin:
Know where you came from,
and where you are going,
and before Whom you will one day
have to give a judgment and an accounting.
chunks.explain: You will have to explain everything you did.

chunks.en: Where did you come from?
From a smelly drop.
And where are you going?
To a place of dust, worms and maggots.
And before Whom will you one day
have to give a judgment and an accounting?
Before the King of all kings,
the Holy One, blessed is He.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Chanina teaches us to daven for the government, because it keeps order. Rabbi Chanina ben Teradyon teaches that when people sit together and talk words of Torah, the Shechinah is with them, and even one person who learns alone gets a reward.

chunks.en: Rabbi Chanina, the assistant of the Kohanim, says:
Daven for the peace of the government,
because if not for the fear of it,
people would swallow each other alive.
Rabbi Chanina ben Teradyon says:

chunks.he: שְׁנַיִם שֶׁיּוֹשְׁבִין וְאֵין בֵּינֵיהֶן דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
chunks.en: Two people who sit and there are no words of Torah between them,
that is a seat of scoffers,
chunks.explain: People who make fun of serious things.

chunks.en: as it says (Tehillim 1): And in the seat
of scoffers he did not sit.
But two who sit
and there are words of Torah between them,
the Shechinah rests among them,
as it says (Malachi 3): Then those who fear

chunks.he: יְיָ אִישׁ אֶל רֵעֵהוּ וַיַּקְשֵׁב יְיָ
chunks.en: Hashem spoke to each other, and Hashem listened,

chunks.he: וַיִּשְׁמָע וַיִּכָּתֵב סֵפֶר זִכָּרוֹן לְפָנָיו לְיִרְאֵי
chunks.en: and heard, and a book of remembrance was written before Him for those who fear
Hashem and those who think about His Name.

words.en: and for those who think of

chunks.en: This only teaches about two.

chunks.he: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֲפִלּוּ אֶחָד שֶׁיּוֹשֵׁב וְעוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה,
chunks.en: How do we know that even one who sits and learns Torah,

chunks.he: שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא קוֹבֵעַ לוֹ שָׂכָר,
chunks.en: the Holy One, blessed is He, sets a reward for him?
As it says (Eichah 3): He sits alone
and is quiet, because he took it upon himself.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Shimon teaches that when three people eat together and say words of Torah, it is as if they ate from Hashem's table. If they do not, it is like eating offerings to idols.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says:
Three people who ate at one table
and did not say words of Torah at it,
it is as if they ate from offerings to dead idols,
as it says (Yeshayah 28): For all the tables
are full of a dirty mess, without Hashem.
But three who ate at
one table and said words of Torah at it,
it is as if they ate from the table of
Hashem, blessed is He,
as it says (Yechezkel 41): And he said to me:
This is the table that is before Hashem.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Chanina ben Chachinai warns that being awake at night, walking alone on the road, or letting your mind be empty of Torah puts a person in danger.

chunks.en: Rabbi Chanina ben Chachinai says:
One who is awake at night, and one who walks on the road
alone, and one who turns his heart to emptiness,
chunks.explain: He thinks about nothing instead of Torah.

chunks.en: he puts his life in danger.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Nechunya ben HaKanah teaches that someone who takes on the yoke of Torah is freed from other burdens, but someone who throws off the Torah gets other burdens put on him.

chunks.en: Rabbi Nechunya ben HaKanah says:
Whoever takes on himself the yoke of Torah,
chunks.explain: A yoke is a wooden bar that lets an animal pull a load.

chunks.en: they remove from him the yoke of the government
and the yoke of earning a living.
And whoever throws off the yoke of Torah,
they put on him the yoke of the government
and the yoke of earning a living.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Chalafta teaches that when people learn Torah together, the Shechinah is with them. This is true for ten, five, three, two, and even one person.

chunks.en: Rabbi Chalafta ben Dosa
of Kfar Chananyah says:
Ten people who sit and learn Torah,
the Shechinah rests among them,
as it says (Tehillim 82): Hashem
stands in the assembly of Hashem.
chunks.explain: An assembly is ten people.

chunks.en: And how do we know even five?
As it says (Amos 9): And His group
He set up on the earth.
And how do we know even three?
As it says (Tehillim 82): Among the judges He judges.
chunks.explain: A beis din has three judges.

chunks.en: And how do we know even two?
As it says (Malachi 3): Then spoke
those who fear Hashem, each to his friend,
and Hashem listened and heard, and so on.
And how do we know even one?
As it says (Shemos 20): In every place where

chunks.he: אַזְכִּיר אֶת שְׁמִי אָבֹא אֵלֶיךָ וּבֵרַכְתִּיךָ:
chunks.en: I let My Name be mentioned, I will come to you and bless you.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Elazar teaches to give to Hashem from what is His, because everything we have belongs to Him. Rabbi Shimon warns not to stop learning Torah to admire nature.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar of Barsosa says:
Give Him from what is His,
because you and what is yours are His.
And so it says about Dovid (Divrei
HaYamim I 29): For from You
comes everything, and from Your hand we gave to You.
Rabbi Shimon says:
One who walks on the road and learns,
and stops his learning and says:
How beautiful is this tree!
And how beautiful is this field!

chunks.he: מַעֲלֶה עָלָיו הַכָּתוּב כְּאִלּוּ מִתְחַיֵּב בְּנַפְשׁוֹ:
chunks.en: the Torah counts it against him as if he put his life in danger.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Meir teaches that a person must be very careful not to forget his learning on purpose, but someone who forgets because it was too hard is not to blame.

chunks.en: Rabbi Dostai, son of Rabbi Yannai,
in the name of Rabbi Meir, says:
Whoever forgets one thing from his learning,

chunks.he: מַעֲלֶה עָלָיו הַכָּתוּב כְּאִלּוּ מִתְחַיֵּב בְּנַפְשׁוֹ,
chunks.en: the Torah counts it against him as if he put his life in danger,
as it says (Devarim 4): Only guard yourself

chunks.he: וּשְׁמֹר נַפְשְׁךָ מְאֹד פֶּן תִּשְׁכַּח אֶת
chunks.en: and guard your soul very much, so that you do not forget
the things that your eyes saw.
I might think even if his learning was too hard for him,
so the Torah says (there): And so that they do not leave
your heart all the days of your life.
So he is not guilty
until he sits and removes them from his heart.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa teaches that wisdom lasts when a person's fear of sin comes first, and when his good deeds are more than his wisdom.

chunks.en: Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa says:
Anyone whose fear of sin comes before his wisdom,
his wisdom will last.
And anyone whose wisdom comes before his fear of sin,
his wisdom will not last.
He used to say:
Anyone whose deeds are more than his wisdom,
his wisdom will last.
And anyone whose wisdom is more than his deeds,
his wisdom will not last.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Chanina teaches that if people are pleased with someone, Hashem is pleased with him too. Rabbi Dosa warns that sleeping late, drinking wine at midday, silly talk and sitting with people who don't learn take a person out of the world.

chunks.en: He used to say:
Anyone whom people are pleased with,
Hashem is pleased with him.

chunks.he: וְכָל שֶׁאֵין רוּחַ הַבְּרִיּוֹת נוֹחָה הֵימֶנּוּ,
chunks.en: And anyone whom people are not pleased with,
Hashem is not pleased with him.
Rabbi Dosa ben Harkinas says:
Sleeping late in the morning,
and wine in the middle of the day,
and children's chatter,

chunks.he: וִישִׁיבַת בָּתֵּי כְנֵסִיּוֹת שֶׁל עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ,
chunks.en: and sitting in the meeting places of unlearned people,
take a person out of the world.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Elazar HaModai lists people who lose their share in the World to Come, like one who embarrasses his friend in public, even if he has Torah and good deeds.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar HaModai says:
One who treats holy things as ordinary,
and one who looks down on the Yomim Tovim,

words.en: and the one who looks down on

chunks.en: and one who embarrasses his friend in public,

words.en: and the one who makes white
words.note: Embarrasses, so his face goes pale.

chunks.en: and one who breaks the covenant of Avraham
our father, peace be upon him,
and one who explains the Torah against the halachah,
even though he has
Torah and good deeds in his hand,
he has no share in the World to Come.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Yishmael teaches to be quick to serve a great person, to be pleasant to a young person, and to greet everyone happily.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yishmael says:
Be quick to serve a leader,
and easy-going with a young person,

words.note: Someone with black hair, not yet gray.

chunks.he: וֶהֱוֵי מְקַבֵּל אֶת כָּל הָאָדָם בְּשִׂמְחָה:
chunks.en: and greet every person with joy.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Akiva teaches that joking around leads to bad behavior, and that fences protect good things: tradition protects the Torah, maaser protects wealth, promises protect self-control, and silence protects wisdom.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says:
Joking and lightheadedness
lead a person to forbidden behavior.
The Mesorah is a fence for the Torah.

words.note: The tradition of how the words of the Torah are written.

chunks.en: Maaser is a fence for wealth.
Promises are a fence for holding back.
A fence for wisdom is silence.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Akiva teaches that Hashem loves people, who were made in His image. He loves the Jewish people, who are called His children and who were given the precious Torah.

chunks.en: He used to say:
Man is dear, because he was created in Hashem's image.

chunks.he: חִבָּה יְתֵרָה נוֹדַעַת לוֹ שֶׁנִּבְרָא בְצֶלֶם,
chunks.en: It is an extra love that it was told to him that he was created in Hashem's image,
as it says (Bereishis 9): For in the image
of Hashem He made man.
Yisrael are dear, because they are called Hashem's children.
It is an extra love that it was told to them
that they are called Hashem's children,
as it says (Devarim 14): Children
are you to Hashem your G-d.

chunks.he: חֲבִיבִין יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנִּתַּן לָהֶם כְּלִי חֶמְדָּה.
chunks.en: Yisrael are dear, because they were given a precious tool.

chunks.he: חִבָּה יְתֵרָה נוֹדַעַת לָהֶם שֶׁנִּתַּן לָהֶם
chunks.en: It is an extra love that it was told to them that they were given
a precious tool, with which the world was created,
as it says (Mishlei 4): For
a good teaching I have given you,
do not leave My Torah.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Akiva teaches that Hashem sees everything, yet we are free to choose. Hashem judges the world with goodness, according to most of our deeds.

chunks.en: Everything is seen,
yet permission is given,
chunks.explain: We are free to choose good or bad.

chunks.en: and the world is judged with goodness.
And everything is by the most of the deeds.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Akiva compares the world to a store where everything is given on loan. Hashem keeps track of everything, people are paid back fairly, and at the end, everything is ready for the great feast for the tzaddikim.

chunks.en: He used to say:
Everything is given as a loan with a promise,
and a net is spread over all living things.
The store is open,
and the storekeeper gives credit,
chunks.explain: He lets you take now and pay later.

chunks.en: and the account book is open,
and the hand writes,
and whoever wants to borrow can come and borrow,
and the collectors go around always, every day,

chunks.he: וְנִפְרָעִין מִן הָאָדָם מִדַּעְתּוֹ וְשֶׁלֹּא מִדַּעְתּוֹ,
chunks.en: and collect from a person whether he knows it or not,
and they have what to lean on,
chunks.explain: They have the account book to show.

chunks.en: and the judgment is a true judgment,
and everything is ready for the feast.

words.note: The reward of the tzaddikim in the World to Come.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah teaches that Torah and good manners, wisdom and fear of Hashem, all need each other. Someone whose deeds are more than his wisdom is like a tree with strong roots that no wind can knock down.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah says:
If there is no Torah,
there are no good manners.
If there are no good manners,
there is no Torah.
If there is no wisdom,
there is no fear of Hashem.
If there is no fear of Hashem,
there is no wisdom.
If there is no understanding,
there is no knowledge.
If there is no knowledge,
there is no understanding.
If there is no flour,
chunks.explain: Without food, a person cannot learn.

chunks.en: there is no Torah.
If there is no Torah,
there is no flour.
He used to say:
Anyone whose wisdom is more than his deeds,
what is he like?
Like a tree with many branches and few roots,

chunks.he: וְהָרוּחַ בָּאָה וְעוֹקַרְתּוֹ וְהוֹפַכְתּוֹ עַל פָּנָיו,
chunks.en: and the wind comes and pulls it up and turns it over on its face,
as it says (Yirmiyah 17): And he will be like a lonely bush in the desert,

chunks.he: וְלֹא יִרְאֶה כִּי יָבוֹא טוֹב וְשָׁכַן
chunks.en: and he will not see when good comes, and he will live

chunks.he: חֲרֵרִים בַּמִּדְבָּר אֶרֶץ מְלֵחָה וְלֹא תֵשֵׁב.
chunks.en: in dry places in the wilderness, a salty land where no one lives.
But anyone whose deeds are more than his wisdom,
what is he like?
Like a tree with few branches and many roots,

chunks.he: שֶׁאֲפִלּוּ כָל הָרוּחוֹת שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם בָּאוֹת וְנוֹשְׁבוֹת
chunks.en: that even if all the winds in the world come and blow
at it, they cannot move it from its place,
as it says (there): And he will be like a tree planted by

chunks.he: מַיִם וְעַל יוּבַל יְשַׁלַּח שָׁרָשָׁיו וְלֹא
chunks.en: the water, that sends its roots by a stream, and will not
see when heat comes,
and its leaves will be fresh,
and in a year of no rain it will not worry,
and it will not stop making fruit.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Eliezer ben Chisma teaches that even hard, detailed laws are the main body of halachah, while counting the seasons and number puzzles are like extras around wisdom.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer ben Chisma says:
The laws of bird korbanos and the laws of niddah,

words.note: Laws about a kind of tumah.

chunks.en: they are the main body of the halachos.
Counting the seasons and number counting

words.note: Counting the times of the sun and moon.

chunks.en: are the side dishes of wisdom.

mishnayos.summary: Ben Zoma teaches who is truly wise, strong, rich and honored: one who learns from everyone, controls his yetzer hara, is happy with what he has, and honors other people.

chunks.en: Ben Zoma says:
Who is wise?
One who learns from every person,
as it says (Tehillim 119): From all my teachers
I became wise, because Your laws are what I talk about.
Who is strong?
One who controls his yetzer hara,
as it says (Mishlei 16): Better is one who is slow to anger
than a strong man, and one who rules his spirit than one who captures a city.
Who is rich?
One who is happy with his share,
as it says (Tehillim 128): The work of your hands
when you eat it, you are fortunate and it is good for you.
You are fortunate in this world,
and it is good for you
in the World to Come.
Who is honored?
One who honors people,
as it says (Shmuel I 2): For
those who honor Me I will honor, and those who look down on Me will be made small.

mishnayos.summary: Ben Azzai teaches to run to do even a small mitzvah and to run away from aveiros, because one mitzvah leads to another and one aveirah leads to another.

chunks.en: Ben Azzai says:
Run to do a light mitzvah just as you would a heavy one,
and run away from aveirah.
Because a mitzvah pulls along another mitzvah,
and an aveirah pulls along another aveirah.
Because the reward of a mitzvah
is a mitzvah, and the payment for an aveirah is an aveirah.

mishnayos.summary: Ben Azzai teaches not to look down on any person or on anything, because every person has his time and every thing has its place.

chunks.en: He used to say:
Do not look down on any person,
and do not push away anything as impossible,

chunks.he: שֶׁאֵין לְךָ אָדָם שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שָׁעָה
chunks.en: because there is no person who does not have his moment,

chunks.he: וְאֵין לְךָ דָבָר שֶׁאֵין לוֹ מָקוֹם:
chunks.en: and there is no thing that does not have its place.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Levitas teaches to be very humble. Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka warns that one who makes Hashem's Name disgraced in secret is punished in public, whether he did it by accident or on purpose.

chunks.en: Rabbi Levitas of Yavneh says:
Be very, very humble,
because what waits for a person in the end is worms.
Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka says:
Whoever disgraces the Name of Heaven in secret,
they punish him in public.

chunks.he: אֶחָד שׁוֹגֵג וְאֶחָד מֵזִיד בְּחִלּוּל הַשֵּׁם:
chunks.en: Whether by accident or on purpose, it is the same when it comes to disgracing Hashem's Name.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Yishmael teaches that one who learns in order to teach and to do gets help to do it all. Rabbi Tzadok warns not to use the Torah to make yourself great or to earn money.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yishmael his son says:
One who learns Torah in order to teach,
they help him to learn and to teach.
And one who learns in order to do,

chunks.he: מַסְפִּיקִין בְּיָדוֹ לִלְמֹד וּלְלַמֵּד לִשְׁמֹר וְלַעֲשׂוֹת.
chunks.en: they help him to learn, to teach, to guard and to do.
Rabbi Tzadok says:
Do not make the words of Torah a crown to make yourself great with,
and not an ax to dig with.
chunks.explain: Do not use the Torah as a tool to earn money.

chunks.en: And so Hillel used to say:
And one who uses the crown of Torah for himself
passes away. So you learned:
whoever gets benefit from words of Torah
takes away his life from the world.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Yosi teaches that one who honors the Torah will be honored by people, and one who disgraces the Torah will be disgraced by people.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosi says:
Whoever honors the Torah,
he himself will be honored by people.
And whoever disgraces the Torah,
he himself will be disgraced by people.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Yishmael teaches that a judge who avoids judging when he can keeps away from many problems, but one who rushes to rule is foolish, wicked and proud.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yishmael his son says:
One who holds himself back from judging,
chunks.explain: He tries to make peace between people instead.

chunks.he: פּוֹרֵק מִמֶּנּוּ אֵיבָה וְגָזֵל וּשְׁבוּעַת שָׁוְא.
chunks.en: removes from himself hatred, stealing, and a false oath.
And one who is too sure of himself when he rules,

words.en: and the one who is proud

chunks.en: is foolish, wicked and proud.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Yishmael teaches not to judge alone, because only Hashem judges alone, and not to force others to accept your opinion.

chunks.en: He used to say:
Do not judge alone,
because no one judges alone except the One.
And do not say: Accept my opinion,
because they are allowed to, and not you.
chunks.explain: The other judges, who are the majority, can decide.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Yonasan teaches that one who keeps the Torah when he is poor will in the end keep it when he is rich, and one who stops learning because he is rich will in the end stop because he is poor.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yonasan says:
Whoever keeps the Torah when he is poor,
in the end will keep it when he is rich.
And whoever stops keeping the Torah because he is rich,
in the end will stop it because he is poor.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Meir teaches to do less business and more Torah, to be humble before everyone, and that Hashem has a big reward for anyone who works hard at Torah.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says:
Do less business,
and be busy with Torah.

chunks.he: וֶהֱוֵי שְׁפַל רוּחַ בִּפְנֵי כָל אָדָם.
chunks.en: And be humble before every person.
And if you stopped learning Torah,
you will have many things that stop you.
chunks.explain: One wasted moment leads to more.

chunks.en: And if you worked hard in Torah,

chunks.he: יֶשׁ לוֹ שָׂכָר הַרְבֵּה לִתֶּן לָךְ:
chunks.en: He has a lot of reward to give you.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov teaches that each mitzvah makes a friend who speaks up for us, and each aveirah makes an accuser. Rabbi Yochanan HaSandlar teaches that a gathering for the sake of Heaven will last.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
One who does one mitzvah
gets for himself one defender.
chunks.explain: Someone who speaks up for him before Hashem.

chunks.en: And one who does one aveirah
gets for himself one accuser.
Teshuvah and good deeds
are like a shield against punishment.
Rabbi Yochanan HaSandlar says:
Every gathering that is for the sake of Heaven
will in the end last.
And one that is not for the sake of Heaven
will not last in the end.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Elazar ben Shamua teaches to honor your student like yourself, your friend like your teacher, and your teacher like Hashem.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar ben Shamua says:

chunks.he: יְהִי כְבוֹד תַּלְמִידְךָ חָבִיב עָלֶיךָ כְּשֶׁלְּךָ,
chunks.en: Let your student's honor be as dear to you as your own,
and your friend's honor like the respect for your teacher,
and the respect for your teacher like the fear of Heaven.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Yehudah teaches to be careful when you learn, because a mistake in learning can lead to doing wrong. Rabbi Shimon teaches that there are three crowns, but a good name is above them all.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says:
Be careful in your learning,
because a mistake in learning counts as doing it on purpose.
Rabbi Shimon says:
There are three crowns:

chunks.he: כֶּתֶר תּוֹרָה וְכֶתֶר כְּהֻנָּה וְכֶתֶר מַלְכוּת,
chunks.en: the crown of Torah, and the crown of the Kohanim, and the crown of kingship,

chunks.he: וְכֶתֶר שֵׁם טוֹב עוֹלֶה עַל גַּבֵּיהֶן:
chunks.en: but the crown of a good name is above them all.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Nehorai teaches to go to a place of Torah, and not to think the Torah will come to you by itself or that you can understand it alone without friends.

chunks.en: Rabbi Nehorai says:
Move yourself to a place of Torah,
and do not say that it will come after you,
that your friends will make it last in your hand.
chunks.explain: You need friends to learn with.

chunks.en: And do not lean on your own understanding (Mishlei 3).

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Yannai teaches that we cannot understand why wicked people may have it good and tzaddikim may suffer. Rabbi Masya teaches to greet everyone first and to be a tail to lions rather than a head to foxes.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yannai says:
It is not in our hands to understand the calm of the wicked,
nor the sufferings of the tzaddikim.
Rabbi Masya ben Charash says:
Be the first to greet every person.
And be a tail to lions,
chunks.explain: Be the smallest among great people.

chunks.en: and do not be a head to foxes.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Yaakov teaches that this world is like a front hall before the World to Come. We should get ready here so we can enter the palace.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yaakov says:
This world is like a front hall
before the World to Come.
Get yourself ready in the front hall,
so that you can go into the palace.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Yaakov teaches that one hour of teshuvah and good deeds in this world is better than all of the World to Come, and one hour of calm in the World to Come is better than all of this world.

chunks.en: He used to say:
One hour of teshuvah
and good deeds in this world
is better than all the life of the World to Come.
And one hour of
calm of the spirit in the World to Come
is better than all the life of this world.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar teaches to choose the right time: don't try to calm a friend when he is angry, don't comfort him right after someone died, and don't look at him when he is embarrassed.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:

chunks.he: אַל תְּרַצֶּה אֶת חֲבֵרְךָ בִשְׁעַת כַּעֲסוֹ,
chunks.en: Do not try to calm your friend when he is angry,

chunks.he: וְאַל תְּנַחֲמֶנּוּ בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁמֵּתוֹ מֻטָּל לְפָנָיו,
chunks.en: and do not comfort him while his dead relative is lying before him,
and do not ask him about his promise at the time he makes it,
chunks.explain: Wait until he can listen calmly.

chunks.en: and do not try to see him when he has done something wrong.
chunks.explain: He will be embarrassed.

mishnayos.summary: Shmuel HaKatan teaches, using a pasuk, not to be happy when your enemy falls.

chunks.en: Shmuel HaKatan says:
(Mishlei 24) When your enemy falls, do not
be happy, and when he trips, let your heart not be glad,
or else Hashem will see, and it will be bad
in His eyes, and He will turn His anger away from him.

mishnayos.summary: Elisha ben Avuyah teaches that learning as a child stays strong, like ink on new paper. Rebbi teaches not to look at the container but at what is inside it.

chunks.en: Elisha ben Avuyah says:
One who learns as a child, what is he like?
Like ink written on new paper.
And one who learns as an old man, what is he like?
Like ink written on erased paper.
Rabbi Yosi bar Yehudah
of Kfar HaBavli says:

chunks.he: הַלּוֹמֵד מִן הַקְּטַנִּים לְמַה הוּא דוֹמֶה,
chunks.en: One who learns from young people, what is he like?

chunks.he: לְאֹכֵל עֲנָבִים קֵהוֹת וְשׁוֹתֶה יַיִן מִגִּתּוֹ.
chunks.en: Like one who eats unripe grapes and drinks wine straight from the press.

chunks.he: וְהַלּוֹמֵד מִן הַזְּקֵנִים לְמַה הוּא דוֹמֶה,
chunks.en: And one who learns from old people, what is he like?

chunks.he: לְאֹכֵל עֲנָבִים בְּשֵׁלוֹת וְשׁוֹתֶה יַיִן יָשָׁן.
chunks.en: Like one who eats ripe grapes and drinks old wine.
Rebbi says:
Do not look at the jug,
but at what is inside it.
There is a new jug full of old wine,
and an old one that does not even have new wine in it.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Elazar HaKappar teaches that jealousy, wanting too much, and chasing honor take a person out of the world.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar HaKappar says:
Jealousy, wanting too much, and chasing honor,
take a person out of the world.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Elazar HaKappar teaches that Hashem made us and will judge us fairly, with no forgetting and no bribes. We should not think we can escape by dying, because everything happens by Hashem's will.

chunks.en: He used to say:
Those who are born will die,
and the dead will come back to life,
and those who live will be judged.
To know, to tell others, and to make it known that He is G-d,
He is the One Who forms,
He is the Creator,
He is the One Who understands,
He is the Judge,
He is the Witness,
He is the One Who brings the case,
and He will one day judge.
Blessed is He,
that before Him there is no wrongdoing,
and no forgetting,
and no favoring anyone,
and no taking bribes,
because everything is His.
And know that everything goes by the account.
And do not let your yetzer hara promise you that the grave
is a place to escape to.
Because against your will you are formed,
and against your will you are born,
and against your will you live,
and against your will you die,
and against your will you will one day give
a judgment and an accounting before the King of all
kings, the Holy One, blessed is He.

mishnayos.summary: Hashem created the world with ten sayings, even though He could have used one. This shows how much it matters: the wicked who ruin the world are punished more, and the tzaddikim who keep it going get a bigger reward.

chunks.en: The world was created with ten sayings.
chunks.explain: Ten times the Torah says "And Hashem said" in the story of creation.

chunks.en: And what does this teach us?
Couldn't it have been created with one saying?
But it is to punish the wicked who ruin
the world that was created with ten sayings,
and to give a good reward to the tzaddikim who keep up
the world that was created with ten sayings.

mishnayos.summary: There were ten generations from Adam to Noach, and ten from Noach to Avraham. This shows how patient Hashem is. Avraham came and got the reward of all of them.

chunks.en: There were ten generations from Adam until Noach,
to show how patient Hashem is,

chunks.he: שֶׁכָּל הַדּוֹרוֹת הָיוּ מַכְעִיסִין וּבָאִין עַד
chunks.en: because all the generations kept making Him angry, until
He brought the waters of the Flood on them.
There were ten generations from Noach until Avraham,
to show how patient Hashem is,
because all the generations kept making Him angry,
until Avraham came and took
for himself the reward of all of them.

mishnayos.summary: Avraham Avinu was tested ten times and passed every test. This shows how much he loved Hashem.

chunks.en: Avraham Avinu was tested with ten tests,
peace be upon him, and he stood strong in all of them,
to show how great the love of
Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him, was.

mishnayos.summary: Hashem did ten miracles for our fathers in Mitzrayim and ten at the sea, and brought ten makkos on the Mitzrim in Mitzrayim and ten at the sea. Our fathers tested Hashem ten times in the desert.

chunks.en: Ten miracles were done for our fathers
in Mitzrayim, and ten at the sea.

chunks.he: עֶשֶׂר מַכּוֹת הֵבִיא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
chunks.en: Ten makkos the Holy One, blessed is He, brought

chunks.he: עַל הַמִּצְרִיִּים בְּמִצְרַיִם וְעֶשֶׂר עַל הַיָּם.
chunks.en: on the Mitzrim in Mitzrayim, and ten at the sea.
With ten tests our fathers tested
Hashem, blessed is He, ten times in the desert,
as it says (Bamidbar 14): And they tested Me these
ten times and did not listen to My voice.

mishnayos.summary: Ten miracles happened all the time in the Beis HaMikdash. For example, the korban meat never went bad, no fly was seen where the animals were prepared, and there was always room for everyone.

chunks.he: עֲשָׂרָה נִסִּים נַעֲשׂוּ לַאֲבוֹתֵינוּ בְּבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ.
chunks.en: Ten miracles were done for our fathers in the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.he: לֹא הִפִּילָה אִשָּׁה מֵרֵיחַ בְּשַׂר הַקֹּדֶשׁ,
chunks.en: No woman expecting a baby was ever harmed by the smell of the holy meat,
and the holy meat never went bad,
and no fly was seen in the place where the animals were prepared,
and it never happened that the Kohen
Gadol became tamei on Yom Kippur,
and the rain never put out the fire
of the wood on the mizbe'ach,

words.note: The pile of wood on the mizbe'ach.

chunks.he: וְלֹא נָצְחָה הָרוּחַ אֶת עַמּוּד הֶעָשָׁן,
chunks.en: and the wind never pushed away the pillar of smoke,
and nothing was ever found unfit in the Omer,

words.note: The barley offering brought on the second day of Pesach.

chunks.en: or in the Two Breads, or in the Lechem HaPanim.
They stood squeezed together, yet bowed with plenty of room,

chunks.he: וְלֹא הִזִּיק נָחָשׁ וְעַקְרָב בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם מֵעוֹלָם,
chunks.en: and no snake or scorpion ever hurt anyone in Yerushalayim,
and no person ever said to his friend: There is not
enough room for me to sleep over in Yerushalayim.

mishnayos.summary: Ten special things were created at the very end of the six days of creation, just before the first Shabbos, like the mouth of the earth that swallowed Korach, the mann, and the Luchos.

chunks.en: Ten things were created on Erev
Shabbos at twilight,
and these are they:
the mouth of the earth,
chunks.explain: It opened to swallow Korach.

chunks.en: and the mouth of the well,
chunks.explain: Miriam's well in the desert.

chunks.en: and the mouth of the donkey,
chunks.explain: Bilam's donkey that talked.

chunks.en: and the rainbow, and the mann,
and the staff, and the shamir,

words.note: A tiny creature that could cut stone.

chunks.en: and the writing, and the writing tool,
and the Luchos. And some say:
also the harmful spirits,
and Moshe's grave,
and the ram of Avraham Avinu.
And some say:
also the tongs, which are made with tongs.
chunks.explain: Someone had to make the very first tongs.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah lists seven ways a wise person behaves: he lets someone greater speak first, doesn't interrupt, answers carefully, and admits the truth. A foolish person does the opposite.

chunks.en: There are seven things in a foolish person, and seven in a wise person.
A wise person does not speak before someone
who is greater than him in wisdom and in years,
and he does not break into his friend's words,
and he does not rush to answer,
he asks about the topic and answers according to the halachah,
and he talks about the first thing first
and about the last thing last,
and about what he did not hear,
he says: I did not hear.
And he admits the truth.
And the opposite of these are in the foolish person.

mishnayos.summary: Seven kinds of punishment come to the world for seven kinds of aveiros. For example, when people don't give maaser, there is hunger.

chunks.en: Seven kinds of punishments come to the world
for seven main kinds of aveirah.
When some give maaser and some do not give maaser,
a hunger of dryness comes,
some are hungry and some are full.
When they decided not to give maaser,

chunks.he: רָעָב שֶׁל מְהוּמָה וְשֶׁל בַּצֹּרֶת בָּאָה.
chunks.en: a hunger of confusion and of dryness comes.
And when they decided not to take challah,

words.note: A piece of dough given to the Kohen.

chunks.en: a hunger that destroys comes.

chunks.he: דֶּבֶר בָּא לָעוֹלָם עַל מִיתוֹת הָאֲמוּרוֹת
chunks.en: A plague comes to the world for deaths said
in the Torah that were not given to beis din,
chunks.explain: Punishments that Hashem Himself gives.

chunks.en: and for the fruits of Shemittah.
chunks.explain: Using the fruit of the seventh year the wrong way.

chunks.he: חֶרֶב בָּאָה לָעוֹלָם עַל עִנּוּי הַדִּין,
chunks.en: The sword comes to the world for slowing down justice,
and for twisting justice,
and for those who teach the Torah against the halachah.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah lists more punishments and their reasons, like wild animals for false oaths, and exile for the worst aveiros. It also lists the times when plague grows, because people did not give the poor what belongs to them.

chunks.en: Wild animals come to the world
for false oaths,
and for disgracing Hashem's Name.
Exile comes to the world for
those who serve idols,
and for forbidden relationships,
and for killing,
and for not letting the land rest.
At four times the plague grows:
in the fourth year, and in the seventh year,
and right after the seventh year,

words.en: and at the going out of

chunks.en: and right after Sukkos of each and every year.

words.en: and at the going out of

chunks.en: In the fourth year, because of maaser for the poor of the third year.
In the seventh year, because of maaser for the poor of the sixth year.
And right after the seventh year,

words.en: and at the going out of

chunks.en: because of the fruits of the seventh year.
And right after Sukkos of each and every year,

words.en: and at the going out of

chunks.en: because of stealing gifts of the poor.

mishnayos.summary: There are four kinds of people when it comes to sharing what they own. The one who says "mine is yours and yours is yours" is a chasid, and the one who says "yours is mine and mine is mine" is wicked.

chunks.en: There are four kinds of people.
One who says: Mine is mine and yours is yours,
this is an in-between way.
And some say:
this is the way of Sedom.
chunks.explain: The people of Sedom did not want to share anything.

chunks.en: Mine is yours and yours is mine:
an unlearned person.

words.note: Am ha'aretz: someone who does not understand.

chunks.en: Mine is yours and yours is yours:

chunks.he: חָסִיד. שֶׁלִּי שֶׁלִּי וְשֶׁלְּךָ שֶׁלִּי, רָשָׁע:
chunks.en: a chasid. Mine is mine and yours is mine: a wicked person.

mishnayos.summary: There are four kinds of tempers. Best is someone who is hard to make angry and easy to calm down; worst is someone who gets angry easily and is hard to calm down.

chunks.en: There are four kinds of tempers.
Easy to anger and easy to calm down:
his gain is lost by his loss.
Hard to anger and hard to calm down:
his loss is made up by his gain.
Hard to anger and easy to calm down:

chunks.he: חָסִיד. נוֹחַ לִכְעֹס וְקָשֶׁה לִרְצוֹת, רָשָׁע:
chunks.en: a chasid. Easy to anger and hard to calm down: wicked.

mishnayos.summary: There are four kinds of students. Best is one who learns quickly and forgets slowly; worst is one who learns slowly and forgets quickly.

chunks.en: There are four kinds of students.
Quick to understand and quick to forget:
his gain is lost by his loss.
Slow to understand and slow to forget:
his loss is made up by his gain.
Quick to understand and slow to forget:
a wise person. Slow to understand and quick to forget:
this is a bad share.

mishnayos.summary: There are four kinds of people who give tzedakah. Best is one who gives and wants others to give too; worst is one who does not give and does not want others to give.

chunks.en: There are four kinds of people who give tzedakah.
One who wants to give himself but does not want others to give:
he has a bad eye toward what belongs to others.
chunks.explain: He is jealous of the mitzvah others would get.

chunks.en: Others should give but he will not give:
he has a bad eye toward what is his own.
chunks.explain: He is stingy with his own money.

chunks.en: He will give and others will give:

chunks.he: חָסִיד. לֹא יִתֵּן וְלֹא יִתְּנוּ אֲחֵרִים, רָשָׁע:
chunks.en: a chasid. He will not give and others will not give: wicked.

mishnayos.summary: There are four kinds of people who go to the beis midrash. Best is one who goes and also does what he learned; worst is one who neither goes nor does.

chunks.en: There are four kinds of people who go to the beis midrash.
One who goes but does not do:
he has the reward for going.
One who does but does not go:
he has the reward for doing.
One who goes and does:

chunks.he: חָסִיד. לֹא הוֹלֵךְ וְלֹא עוֹשֶׂה, רָשָׁע:
chunks.en: a chasid. One who does not go and does not do: wicked.

mishnayos.summary: There are four kinds of students who sit before the Sages: like a sponge, a funnel, a strainer and a sifter. The best is like the sifter, which keeps the good fine flour.

chunks.en: There are four kinds among those who sit before the Sages:
a sponge, and a funnel,
a strainer, and a sifter.
A sponge, which soaks up everything.
chunks.explain: He remembers everything, good and bad.

chunks.en: A funnel, which lets in on this side and lets out on that side.
chunks.explain: It goes in one ear and out the other.

chunks.he: מְשַׁמֶּרֶת, שֶׁמּוֹצִיאָה אֶת הַיַּיִן וְקוֹלֶטֶת אֶת הַשְּׁמָרִים.
chunks.en: A strainer, which lets out the wine and keeps the dregs.
chunks.explain: He keeps what is not important.

chunks.he: וְנָפָה, שֶׁמּוֹצִיאָה אֶת הַקֶּמַח וְקוֹלֶטֶת אֶת הַסֹּלֶת:
chunks.en: And a sifter, which lets out the coarse flour and keeps the fine flour.
chunks.explain: He keeps what is best.

mishnayos.summary: Love that depends on getting something ends when that thing is gone, but love that does not depend on anything lasts forever, like the love of Dovid and Yehonasan.

chunks.en: Any love that depends on something,
when the thing is gone,
the love is gone.
But love that does not depend on anything
is never gone.
Which love depends on something?
This is the love of Amnon and Tamar.
chunks.explain: Amnon's love was only for what he wanted, so it ended.

chunks.en: And which does not depend on anything?
This is the love of Dovid and Yehonasan.

mishnayos.summary: An argument for the sake of Heaven, like the arguments between Hillel and Shammai, will last. An argument not for the sake of Heaven, like that of Korach and his group, will not last.

chunks.en: Any argument that is for the sake of Heaven
will last in the end.
And one that is not for the sake of Heaven
will not last in the end.

chunks.he: אֵיזוֹ הִיא מַחֲלֹקֶת שֶׁהִיא לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם,
chunks.en: Which argument is for the sake of Heaven?
This is the argument of Hillel and Shammai.
And which is not for the sake of Heaven?
This is the argument of Korach and all his group.

mishnayos.summary: Someone who helps many people do good is protected from sin, like Moshe. Someone who makes many people sin is not given the chance to do teshuvah, like Yeravam.

chunks.en: Whoever helps the many do good,
no sin will come through him.
And whoever makes the many sin,
he is not given the chance to do teshuvah.
Moshe did good and helped the many do good,
the merit of the many is hung on him,
as it says (Devarim 33): The righteousness of Hashem
he did, and His laws with Yisrael.
Yeravam sinned and made the many sin,

words.note: A king who led many Jews to serve idols.

chunks.en: the sin of the many is hung on him,
as it says (Melachim I 15): For
the sins of Yeravam (ben Nevat) that
he sinned and that he made Yisrael sin.

mishnayos.summary: The students of Avraham Avinu have a good eye, a humble spirit and a soul that wants little. The students of Bilam have the opposite. Avraham's students enjoy this world and the World to Come.

chunks.en: Whoever has
these three things
is one of the students of Avraham Avinu.
And three other things,
is one of the students of Bilam the wicked.
A good eye,
and a humble spirit,
and a soul that wants little,
is one of the students of Avraham Avinu.
A bad eye,
and a proud spirit,
and a soul that wants too much,
is one of the students of Bilam the wicked.
What is the difference between the students of Avraham
Avinu and the students of Bilam the wicked?
The students of Avraham Avinu

chunks.he: אוֹכְלִין בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וְנוֹחֲלִין בָּעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
chunks.en: eat in this world and inherit the World to Come,
as it says (Mishlei 8): To give an inheritance to those who love Me, there is,
and their treasure houses I will fill.
But the students of Bilam the wicked
inherit Gehinnom and go down to the deepest pit,
as it says (Tehillim 55): And You,
Hashem, will bring them down to the deepest pit,

chunks.he: אַנְשֵׁי דָמִים וּמִרְמָה לֹא יֶחֱצוּ יְמֵיהֶם,
chunks.en: men of blood and lies will not live half their days,
but I will trust in You.

mishnayos.summary: Yehudah ben Teima teaches to be bold like a leopard, light like an eagle, fast like a deer and strong like a lion to do what Hashem wants. He ends with a tefillah that Hashem rebuild Yerushalayim soon.

chunks.en: Yehudah ben Teima says:
Be bold like a leopard,
and light like an eagle,
and fast like a deer,
and strong like a lion,
to do the will of your Father in Heaven.
He used to say:
A bold-faced person goes to Gehinnom,
chunks.explain: Someone with chutzpah.

chunks.en: and a person who feels shame goes to Gan Eden.

chunks.he: יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶיךָ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ שֶׁתִּבְנֶה
chunks.en: May it be Your will, Hashem our G-d, that You build

chunks.he: עִירְךָ בִּמְהֵרָה בְיָמֵינוּ וְתֵן חֶלְקֵנוּ בְתוֹרָתֶךָ:
chunks.en: Your city soon in our days, and give us our share in Your Torah.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah tells the right age for each step of life: five for Chumash, ten for Mishnah, thirteen for mitzvos, and so on, all the way to one hundred.

chunks.en: He used to say:
Five years old for Chumash,
ten for Mishnah,
thirteen for mitzvos,
fifteen for Gemara,
eighteen for the chuppah,
twenty to go after a living,
thirty for strength,
forty for understanding,
fifty for giving advice,
sixty for old age,
seventy for gray hair,
eighty for special strength,

words.note: Special strength to live so long.

chunks.en: ninety to bend over,
a hundred is as if he died
and passed and stopped from the world.

mishnayos.summary: Ben Bag Bag teaches in Aramaic to keep turning over the Torah again and again, because everything is in it, and there is nothing better.

chunks.en: Ben Bag Bag says:
Turn it over and turn it over,
chunks.explain: Learn the Torah again and again.

chunks.en: because everything is in it.
And look into it,
and grow old and gray in it,
and do not move away from it,
because you have no better way than it.

mishnayos.summary: Ben Hei Hei teaches that the reward is as big as the effort.

chunks.en: Ben Hei Hei says:
The reward is according to the effort.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Meir teaches that someone who learns Torah for its own sake earns many good things: he is loved by Hashem and by people, the Torah makes him humble and good, and he becomes like a spring that never stops flowing.

chunks.en: The Sages taught in the language of the Mishnah,
blessed is He Who chose them and their Mishnah.
Rabbi Meir says: Anyone
who learns Torah for its own sake,
earns many things.
And more than that, the whole world
is worth it for him.
chunks.explain: The whole world was worth creating just for him.

chunks.en: He is called a friend,
beloved, he loves Hashem,
he loves people,
he makes Hashem happy,
he makes people happy.
And the Torah dresses him in humility and fear of Hashem,

chunks.he: וּמַכְשַׁרְתּוֹ לִהְיוֹת צַדִּיק וְחָסִיד וְיָשָׁר וְנֶאֱמָן,
chunks.en: and makes him fit to be a tzaddik, a chasid, honest and faithful,
and keeps him far from sin,
and brings him close to merit,

chunks.he: וְנֶהֱנִין מִמֶּנּוּ עֵצָה וְתוּשִׁיָּה בִּינָה וּגְבוּרָה,
chunks.en: and people get from him advice and wisdom, understanding and strength,
as it says (Mishlei 8): Mine is advice
and wisdom, I am understanding, mine is strength.

chunks.he: וְנוֹתֶנֶת לוֹ מַלְכוּת וּמֶמְשָׁלָה וְחִקּוּר דִּין,
chunks.en: And it gives him kingship and rule and the power to judge,
and they show him the secrets of the Torah,

chunks.he: וְנַעֲשֶׂה כְמַעְיָן הַמִּתְגַּבֵּר וּכְנָהָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ פוֹסֵק,
chunks.en: and he becomes like a spring that grows stronger and like a river that never stops,
and he is modest and patient,
and he forgives when people insult him,
and it makes him great and lifts him above all creations.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi teaches that every day a voice from Har Sinai calls out sadly about people who don't learn Torah. Only someone who learns Torah is truly free, and learning Torah lifts a person up.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Every single day a heavenly voice
goes out from Har Chorev and announces and says:

chunks.he: אוֹי לָהֶם לַבְּרִיּוֹת מֵעֶלְבּוֹנָהּ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה.
chunks.en: Woe to people because of the insult to the Torah.
Because anyone who does not learn
Torah is called rejected by Hashem,
as it says (Mishlei 11): A gold ring in the nose
of a pig, a pretty woman who has no sense.
And it says (Shemos 32): And the Luchos were the work
of Hashem, and the writing was the writing of Hashem,
engraved on the Luchos.
Do not read charus, engraved, but cheirus, freedom,
chunks.explain: The words look the same in Hebrew.

chunks.en: because no one is truly free except
one who is busy learning Torah.
And anyone who is busy learning
Torah, he goes up higher,
as it says (Bamidbar 21): And from Mattanah
to Nachaliel, and from Nachaliel to Bamos.
chunks.explain: From the gift of Torah a person goes up high.

mishnayos.summary: One who learns even a tiny bit of Torah from someone must give him honor. Dovid HaMelech learned only two things from Achitofel and still called him his teacher. And real honor is only Torah.

chunks.he: הַלּוֹמֵד מֵחֲבֵרוֹ פֶּרֶק אֶחָד אוֹ הֲלָכָה
chunks.en: One who learns from his friend one perek or one

chunks.he: אַחַת אוֹ פָסוּק אֶחָד אוֹ דִבּוּר
chunks.en: halachah or one pasuk or one
saying or even one letter,
must treat him with honor,
because this is what we found with Dovid, king of Yisrael,
who learned from Achitofel nothing but
only two things,
yet he called him his teacher, his guide and his close friend,
as it says (Tehillim 55): But you,
a man like me, my guide and my close friend.
Isn't this a kal vachomer?
chunks.explain: If it is true for the small case, it is surely true for the big one.

chunks.en: If Dovid, king of Yisrael,

chunks.he: שֶׁלֹּא לָמַד מֵאֲחִיתֹפֶל אֶלָּא שְׁנֵי דְבָרִים
chunks.en: who learned from Achitofel only two things,
still called him his teacher, his guide and his close friend,

chunks.he: הַלּוֹמֵד מֵחֲבֵרוֹ פֶּרֶק אֶחָד אוֹ הֲלָכָה
chunks.en: one who learns from his friend one perek or one

chunks.he: אַחַת אוֹ פָסוּק אֶחָד אוֹ דִבּוּר
chunks.en: halachah or one pasuk or one
saying or even one letter,
how much more and more so
must he treat him with honor.
And there is no honor but Torah,
as it says (Mishlei 3): The wise will inherit honor,
(Mishlei 28) and the wholehearted will inherit good.
And there is no good but Torah,
as it says (Mishlei 4): For a good teaching
I have given you, do not leave My Torah.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches that someone who learns Torah may need to live simply, with little food and comfort, and work hard at Torah. If he does, he will be fortunate in this world and in the World to Come.

chunks.en: This is the way of the Torah:
eat bread with salt,
and drink water in small measure,
and sleep on the ground,
and live a hard life,
and work hard in the Torah.
If you do this,
(Tehillim 128) you are fortunate and it is good for you.
You are fortunate in this world, and it is good
for you in the World to Come.

mishnayos.summary: Do not chase after greatness and honor, and do not wish for the tables of kings, because the Torah's table and crown are greater. Hashem will surely pay you for your work.

chunks.en: Do not look for greatness for yourself,
and do not long for honor.
Do more than you learn.
And do not wish for the table of kings,
because your table is greater than their table,
and your crown is greater than their crown,
and your Employer can be trusted
to pay you the reward for your work.

mishnayos.summary: Torah is greater than being a Kohen or a king. It is gained in forty-eight ways, like listening carefully, being humble and happy, asking and answering, and saying something in the name of the person who said it.

chunks.en: Torah is greater than
the Kehunah and the kingship,
because kingship is gained with thirty special qualities,
and the Kehunah with twenty-four,
and the Torah is gained with forty-eight things.
And these are they:
by learning, by listening with the ear,
by saying it clearly with the lips,
by understanding of the heart,
by thinking deeply in the heart,
by awe, by fear,
by humility, by joy,
by purity, by serving the Sages,
by being careful with friends,
chunks.explain: Learning together and checking each other.

chunks.en: and by sharp discussion with students,

words.en: and by the sharp discussion of

chunks.en: by calm thinking, by Chumash,
by Mishnah, by less business,
by less worldly things,
by less pleasure,
by less sleep,
by less chatter,
by less joking,
by being patient,
by a good heart,
by trusting the Sages,
and by accepting suffering,
one who knows his place,
and is happy with his share,

words.en: and the one who is happy

chunks.en: and makes a fence for his words,
and does not take credit for himself,
beloved, loves Hashem,
loves people,
loves tzedakah,
loves fairness,
loves being corrected,
keeps far from honor,
and is not proud of his learning,
and is not happy to give rulings,
helps carry the burden with his friend,
judges him in a good way,
sets him on the truth,
and sets him on peace,
calms his heart in his learning,
chunks.explain: He learns patiently.

chunks.en: asks and answers,
listens and adds,
one who learns in order to teach,
and one who learns in order to do,
one who makes his teacher wiser,
and one who gets exactly right what he heard,

words.en: and the one who makes exact

chunks.en: and one who says a thing in the name of the one who said it.
So you learned that anyone who says a thing
in the name of the one who said it brings redemption to the world,
as it says (Esther 2): And Esther told
the king in the name of Mordechai.
chunks.explain: That is how Mordechai saved the king, which led to the Purim miracle.

mishnayos.summary: Torah is great, because it gives life to those who keep it in this world and the next. The mishnah brings many pesukim that show how Torah brings life, health, honor and peace.

chunks.en: Torah is great, because it gives life
to those who keep it, in this world and in the World to Come,
as it says (Mishlei 4): For they are life
to those who find them, and healing to all his body.
And it says (there 3): It will be healing
for your body and drink for your bones.
And it says (there 3): A tree of life
is it for those who hold on to it, and those who support it are fortunate.
And it says (there 1): For a wreath
of grace they are for your head, and necklaces for your neck.
And it says (there 4): It will give your head
a wreath of grace, a crown of glory it will give you.
And it says (there 9): For through me your days
will increase, and years of life will be added to you.
And it says (there 3): Long life
is in its right hand, in its left hand riches and honor.
And it says (there): For long life
and years of life and peace they will add to you.
And it says (there): Its ways are ways
of pleasantness, and all its paths are peace.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai teaches that beauty, strength, wealth, honor, wisdom, old age and children are fitting for tzaddikim. All of these were found in Rebbi and his sons.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehudah in the name of
Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says:
Beauty and strength and wealth and honor
and wisdom and old age and gray hair and children
are fitting for tzaddikim and fitting for the world,
as it says (there 16): A crown of glory
is gray hair, found in the way of tzedakah.
And it says (there 20): The glory of young men
is their strength, and the beauty of old men is gray hair.
And it says (there 14): The crown of the wise is their wealth.
And it says (there 17): The crown of old men
is grandchildren, and the glory of children is their fathers.
And it says (Yeshayah 24): And will be ashamed
the moon, and the sun will be embarrassed,
because Hashem of Hosts will rule on Mount
Tziyon and in Yerushalayim, and before His elders will be honor.
Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya says:

chunks.he: אֵלּוּ שֶׁבַע מִדּוֹת שֶׁמָּנוּ חֲכָמִים לַצַּדִּיקִים,
chunks.en: These seven qualities that the Sages counted for tzaddikim,
all of them came true in Rebbi and his sons.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Yosi ben Kisma tells how a man offered him great riches to move to his town, but he said he would live only in a place of Torah, because only Torah and good deeds go with a person after he dies.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosi ben Kisma said:
Once I was walking on the road,
and a man met me,
and he greeted me with shalom,
and I greeted him back with shalom.
He said to me:
Rabbi, what place are you from?
I said to him:
From a big city of Sages
and of scholars am I.
He said to me:
Rabbi, would you like to live with us in our place?
And I will give you a million
gold coins and precious stones and pearls.
I said to him:

chunks.he: בְּנִי, אִם אַתָּה נוֹתֵן לִי כָל כֶּסֶף
chunks.en: My son, even if you give me all the silver
and gold and precious stones and pearls in the world,
I would live only in a place of Torah.
And not only that,

chunks.he: אֶלָּא שֶׁבִּשְׁעַת פְּטִירָתוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם אֵין
chunks.en: but when a person leaves this world, nothing

chunks.he: מְלַוִּין לוֹ לָאָדָם לֹא כֶסֶף וְלֹא
chunks.en: goes along with a person, not silver and not
gold and not precious stones and pearls,
but only Torah and good deeds,
as it says (Mishlei 6): When you walk, it will lead you,
when you lie down, it will guard over you,
and when you wake up, it will talk with you.
When you walk, it will lead you,
in this world,
when you lie down, it will guard over you,
in the grave, and when you wake up, it will talk with you,
in the World to Come.

chunks.he: וְכֵן כָּתוּב בְּסֵפֶר תְּהִלִּים עַל יְדֵי
chunks.en: And so it is written in the book of Tehillim by
Dovid, king of Yisrael (Tehillim 119):
The Torah of Your mouth is better for me
than thousands of gold and silver coins.
And it says (Chaggai 2): Mine is the silver
and Mine is the gold, says Hashem of Hosts.

mishnayos.summary: Hashem made five things especially His own in His world: the Torah, the heavens and earth, Avraham, the Jewish people, and the Beis HaMikdash. The mishnah brings a pasuk for each.

chunks.en: Five special possessions
the Holy One, blessed is He, acquired in His world,
and these are they:
Torah is one possession,
heaven and earth are one possession,
Avraham is one possession,
Yisrael is one possession,
the Beis HaMikdash is one possession.
How do we know Torah?
As it is written (Mishlei 8):
Hashem acquired me as the beginning of His way,
before His works, from long ago.
How do we know heaven and earth are one possession?
As it is written (Yeshayah 66):

chunks.he: כֹּה אָמַר ה' הַשָּׁמַיִם כִּסְאִי וְהָאָרֶץ
chunks.en: So says Hashem: The heavens are My throne and the earth

chunks.he: הֲדֹם רַגְלָי אֵי זֶה בַיִת אֲשֶׁר
chunks.en: is My footstool. Which house

chunks.he: תִּבְנוּ לִי וְאֵי זֶה מָקוֹם מְנוּחָתִי,
chunks.en: can you build for Me, and which place is My resting place?
And it says (Tehillim 104): How many
are Your works, Hashem, You made them all with wisdom,
the earth is full of Your possessions.
How do we know Avraham is one possession?
As it is written (Bereishis 14):
And he blessed him and said: Blessed is Avram to G-d
Most High, Who owns heaven and earth.
How do we know Yisrael is one possession?
As it is written (Shemos 15):
Until Your people cross, Hashem, until
this people that You acquired crosses.
And it says (Tehillim 16): For the holy ones who are in the land,
they and the mighty ones, all My desire is in them.
How do we know the Beis HaMikdash is one possession?
As it is written (Shemos 15):
The place for You to dwell that You made, Hashem,
the Mikdash, Hashem, that Your hands set up.
And it says (Tehillim 78): And He brought them to the border
of His holy place, this mountain that His right hand acquired.

mishnayos.summary: Everything Hashem created, He created for His honor. Rabbi Chananya ben Akashya teaches that Hashem gave Yisrael many mitzvos because He wanted to give them merit.

chunks.en: Everything that the Holy One,
blessed is He, created in His world,
He created only for His honor,
as it says (Yeshayah 43):
Everything that is called by My Name and for My honor,
I created it, I formed it, I also made it.
And it says (Shemos 15):
Hashem will rule forever and ever.
Rabbi Chananya ben Akashya says:
The Holy One, blessed is He, wanted
to give merit to Yisrael,
so He gave them a lot of Torah and mitzvos,
as it says (Yeshayah 42): Hashem wanted,
for the sake of its righteousness, to make the Torah great and glorious.
